advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert detector liveness in `_run_check` (e.g. each kind's census non-empty, or the env registry successfully imported) before trusting an absence-derived `stale`/pass verdict.
evidence: scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_code.py:52-54: `except (OSError, SyntaxError, ValueError): continue` silently drops any unparseable .py file
scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_ci.py:110-111: `except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError): continue` silently drops any unparseable workflow

scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_config.py:112-114: `registry = _load_env_registry(repo_root); if registry is None: return []` — a missing generator yields ZERO env_var sites; all baselined env vars then bucket as `stale` and pass
compare.py:96 docstring: '`stale` alone always passes — a removed mechanism is the outcome the ratchet wants.' — a detector that under-reports is indistinguishable from mass removal

_run_check (check_mechanism_delta.py:159-174) prints counters.summary but never asserts any kind produced a non-empty census; the liveness check exists only in the test (test_mechanism_delta.py:43-48), not in the gate
advisory.finding: The gate fails OPEN: every detector silently skips inputs it cannot read/parse, and a detector that returns fewer (or zero) sites than reality makes the affected mechanisms bucket as `stale`, which always passes. `_run_check` performs no liveness assertion that each detector actually produced entries, so 'the detector never ran / found nothing' is indistinguishable from 'the tree is clean' — and it can hide newly-added mechanisms co-located in the dropped input.
scenarios: scripts/gen_env_registry.py is renamed/removed in a future refactor: detect_env_vars returns [], all 132 env vars bucket stale, gate stays green while a new env var is added in the same change
A workflow YAML gains a syntax error: its steps drop from the census as `stale`; a new run: step added in that file is never seen
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_run_check`, fail (nonzero) when a detector that is expected to be non-empty (env_var, config_key, ci_gate, autouse_fixture, test_helper) returns zero sites, or when `_load_env_registry`/`_config_entries` returns its empty sentinel, so a scan that silently found nothing is distinguishable from a clean tree.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_derived_env_names`/`_literal_sites` surface an error (or always attach a site) when an attributed file is absent, rather than silently dropping the derived env var.
evidence: detect_config.py:96-99: `if not path.is_file(): continue` then `if fallback is None: fallback = path`
detect_config.py:105-107: `if not sites and fallback is not None: sites.append((name, fallback, None))` — when fallback is None the derived var is silently omitted
detect_config.py:63-81: `_derived_env_names` hardcodes attributions to 'src/rebar/config.py' and CONFIG_SECTIONS_RELPATH; a rename of either file drops that whole family with no diagnostic
advisory.finding: A derived env var whose attributed file does not exist is silently dropped from the census. `_literal_sites` only sets `fallback` when a relpath `is_file()`; if none exists it returns `[]`, so the env var yields no site at all — it disappears from detect_env_vars rather than surfacing an error, and would bucket as `stale` (pass) even though the variable is real, settable surface.
scenarios: src/rebar/config.py is renamed: env-channel alias env vars lose their attributed file, get no site, and vanish from the census as `stale`

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the `detect_config_keys` docstring to read 'the non-boolean remainder (what `feature_flag` does not claim)' rather than 'the feature_flag remainder'.
evidence: detect_config.py:168-170: `def detect_config_keys(...): """Section-qualified NON-boolean config keys (the ``feature_flag`` remainder)."""` then `return [site for kind, site in _config_entries(repo_root) if kind == "config_key"]`

Module docstring (detect_config.py:18-22) correctly states: 'feature_flag claims the boolean-coerced keys ... and config_key claims only the non-boolean remainder' — the function docstring contradicts it
advisory.finding: The `detect_config_keys` docstring is inverted/self-contradictory: it says it returns 'NON-boolean config keys (the feature_flag remainder)'. Non-boolean keys are the `config_key` set; the phrase 'the feature_flag remainder' describes the opposite partition half and misleads a reader about which kind claims which keys.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to: "Section-qualified NON-boolean config keys (the remainder after ``feature_flag``)."

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests asserting parse_baseline raises SchemaError for unsorted keys, duplicate members, unknown kind, empty name, non-1/bool value, wrong schema_version, missing/extra top-level fields, and malformed/non-UTF-8 input.
evidence: baseline.py:70-100 `parse_baseline` raises SchemaError for: duplicate members (`_reject_duplicate_members`), non-dict doc, `set(doc) != {"schema_version","mechanisms"}`, wrong `schema_version`, non-dict mechanisms, `keys != sorted(keys)`, and per-key `split_key`/`_validate_presence` (unknown kind, empty name, non-1/bool value)
search_files over tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py for `SchemaError` returned (no matches)
test_baseline_round_trips_canonically (lines 51-57) asserts only the happy round-trip parse of a well-formed document

Named violating inputs the added lines must reject but no test drives: `{"schema_version":1,"mechanisms":{"lock::b":1,"lock::a":1}}` (unsorted keys), `{"schema_version":1,"mechanisms":{"lock::x":2}}` (non-1 value), `{"schema_version":1,"mechanisms":{"bogus::x":1}}` (unknown kind), `{"schema_version":2,"mechanisms":{}}` (wrong version), `{"mechanisms":{}}` (missing field)
advisory.finding: parse_baseline's schema-rejection paths are entirely untested. The module docstring declares that unknown/missing top-level fields, duplicate JSON member names, unsorted keys, an unknown kind, an empty name, a non-1 value, invalid UTF-8 and malformed JSON are all rejected, but no test asserts SchemaError for any of these inputs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized test over each malformed document (unsorted keys, non-1 value, unknown kind, wrong schema_version, missing 'mechanisms', duplicate member) asserting pytest.raises(ratchet.SchemaError) — or the subpackage's SchemaError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests that drive parse_marker/markers_for over real source lines: each separator variant, a marker on the line before the definition, and a filename-glob marker within the first 20 lines.
evidence: markers.py:51-68 parse_marker strips one of `_SEPARATORS = ("—", "--", "-", ":")` from the reason and returns (kind,name,reason); markers.py:76-99 collect_at_line scans `lineno-1` and `lineno-2` (the line-before rule) and collect_in_head scans the first HEAD_LINES=20 lines
search over tests file for `parse_marker`, `harvest`, `collect`, `markers_for`: all (no matches)
test_a_marker_with_a_reason_admits_a_new_mechanism (line 169) and the blank-reason tests (line 176) pass literal dicts to evaluate rather than parsing a `# mechanism-ok:` line from source

Named untested inputs: a source line `# mechanism-ok: lock new.lock -- reason` (ASCII double-dash separator) and a marker placed on the line immediately BEFORE the definition — both are behaviors the added code implements but no test drives
advisory.finding: The real marker-parsing and placement path (parse_marker, collect_at_line, collect_in_head, harvest, markers_for) is never exercised; all marker tests inject a pre-built {key: reason} dict directly into evaluate, so the separator handling and line-before/file-head placement rules are untested.

test_update_stale_refuses_to_write_while_a_regression_stands (line 214) covers only the `has_regression` refusal branch (rc != 0, baseline byte-identical)
search over tests file for `drain_stale`: (no matches) — the drain-and-write success path is exercised nowhere

advisory.finding: The successful _run_update_stale path (drops stale entries and atomically rewrites canonical sorted JSON) is untested; only the regression-refusal branch has a test.
